lines.text: What is an always-on agent? Here's the answer, in under sixty seconds.
It's not actually always on. It sleeps, wakes for a short run to do one job, saves what happened, and goes back to sleep.
Say you want an agent that chases a customer who hasn't answered your quote.
First, everything that wakes it, like your request, goes into one inbox.
Second, a timer makes it proactive. The agent sets itself a follow-up timer for Wednesday, and when it's due, an event lands in the inbox.
Third, memory lives in files, so it outlives each run. The agent keeps an instructions file, a progress file for each task, and a record of what you've already been told.
Last, a risky step like sending the follow-up waits for your approval.
You get the outcome, not a live stream, so a good one starts quiet and earns more of your attention.
